title: ioctl_reset: fd permanently dies with -EIO when sess_reset unsupported
description: When \!ops->sess_reset, ioctl_reset now sets state->error = true before returning -EOPNOTSUPP. This permanently kills the fd: subsequent write() and finalize() calls check state->error and return -EIO, not -EOPNOTSUPP. A user who calls RESET on a provider that doesn't support it has done nothing wrong — they tested a capability, found it absent, and should be able to close the fd cleanly or continue using it (it was finalized, not errored). After this change, the fd is dead after a failed reset attempt, and every subsequent operation returns -EIO with no explanation. The error from RESET (-EOPNOTSUPP) is correct; setting state->error is wrong. Trigger: call RESET on a finalized fd backed by a provider without sess_reset. Bad behavior: fd becomes -EIO dead when it should just not support reset.
